Learn Basic Car Troubleshooting Together

Spend an afternoon in a driveway learning to jump-start a car and change a tyre - then you can help anyone stuck at a roadside.

Cost
Free
Time
Half-day
People
Solo / Duo, Small Group (3-6)
Where
Home, Street / Local Business
Bring
A car, jump leads, and the car's tool kit

Why this matters

A flat battery or a punctured tyre strands people for hours and costs a callout fee, and both are fixable in ten minutes by anyone who's done it once. Being able to stop and help someone at a roadside - particularly at night, or someone who's alone and worried - is a small skill with disproportionate value at the moment it's needed.

How to do it

Find someone in your group who knows how, or work through it together with a good video, and practise on an actual car rather than just watching.

What to learn: - Jump-starting: the correct order for connecting and disconnecting leads. Getting the sequence wrong can damage electronics or cause sparks near a battery. Modern cars and hybrids sometimes have specific procedures - check the manual. - Changing a wheel: locating the spare, jack and locking wheel nut key, positioning the jack on the proper jacking point, and loosening nuts before raising the car. - Checking and topping up oil, coolant and screenwash, and knowing what the warning lights mean. - Checking tyre pressure and tread depth. - What's in your car's tool kit - many people have never opened it.

Safety points that matter: - Never get under a car supported only by a jack. - On a motorway or fast road, don't attempt a roadside wheel change. Get behind the barrier and call for help. - If you're stopping to help a stranger, park safely, use hazards and a hi-vis if you have one, and don't put yourself in traffic.

An afternoon in a driveway with a flask, and everyone leaves able to do something they were previously helpless about.
